detail.purpose: Lets the Internal Platform Admin verify donor and receiver FSSAI licence or registration numbers and keep track of when each one expires. A donor whose number is unverified, expired or mismatched cannot post, and an unregistered receiver never appears in matching.

layout.contents: Heading 'FSSAI Verification' with one line saying that only verified donors can post and only registered receivers can be matched. A count of accounts awaiting verification and a count of licences expiring within 30 days.
Role filter (Donor, Receiver), status filter (Verified, Unverified, Expired, Mismatched), and an 'Expiring within 30 days' toggle. A search box for account name or licence number.

One row per donor or receiver account. Columns: account name (synthetic), role, zone, FSSAI licence or registration number, verification status, expiry date, days left, and the check result (name and address on licence match the account or not). Each row has a 'Verify' button for accounts not yet verified and a 'Re-check' button for verified ones. Rows with status Expired or Mismatched are highlighted.
A list of licences that expire within 30 days, sorted by expiry date soonest first. Each item shows account name, role, expiry date and days left. Items past expiry show 'Posting paused'.

Opens beside the selected row. Shows the number entered, the mocked check result (demo: synthetic numbers), the status it sets, the expiry date, and 'Confirm verification' and 'Reject' buttons. Notes that the live FSSAI portal lookup comes in hardening.

shows.details: Account name, role, zone, licence or registration number, verification status, expiry date, days left, name and address match result. Sorted by status with needs-attention rows first, then by expiry date.
Licences expiring within 30 days, soonest first, with days left. Expired ones show that posting is paused.
Number of accounts awaiting verification, number verified, number expired, number expiring within 30 days.

actions.action: Verify a donor or receiver FSSAI number using the mocked check
actions.result: Status becomes Verified and the expiry date is saved. A verified donor can post; a verified receiver can be matched.

actions.action: Reject a number that is invalid, expired or whose name or address does not match the account
actions.result: Status becomes Unverified or Mismatched with the reason saved. The donor cannot post, or the receiver is kept out of matching.

actions.action: Watch expiry dates in the expiry panel
actions.result: Licences due within 30 days are listed with a reminder. When a licence passes its expiry date, the system pauses that donor's posting the same day.

actions.action: Re-check a verified number
actions.result: The mocked check runs again and the status and expiry date are updated.

links.label: Open account
links.when: When the admin needs to change an account's role, see its details, or deactivate it after a failed or expired verification.

links.label: View flags
links.when: When a donor or receiver with a licence problem has a flagged listing or locked handover waiting for a decision.

states.empty: No accounts yet: 'No donors or receivers to verify yet. Accounts appear here once they are added in Users.'
states.loading: Table shows skeleton rows while the accounts and expiry dates load.
states.error: If the check or the list fails: 'Verification could not be completed. Nothing was changed. Try again.' Status stays as it was.

detail.notes: The demo uses synthetic licence numbers and a mocked check; the live FSSAI portal lookup is planned for hardening. The name and address on the licence must match the account. The verification covers the business, not each dish. The screen must never say that food is safe or certified; the badge 'FSSAI-verified donor' appears on donor profiles elsewhere. Receivers and donors do not use this screen.

/fssai-verification.basis: ["FSSAI Verification","Screen where donor and receiver FSSAI licence or registration numbers are verified and their expiry is tracked.",["Internal Platform Admin"],[["Internal Platform Admin","verify FSSAI numbers for donors and receivers; watch expiry dates"]]]

detail.purpose: Lets the Internal Platform Admin work through flagged listings and locked handovers, check guardrail breaches from the AI agents, and fix offers whose volunteer ETA is at risk. Only the admin uses this screen.

layout.contents: Heading 'Flag review' with a one-line note: 'Decide each flag, review guardrail breaches and fix at-risk pickups.' Three tabs below: 'Flags', 'Guardrail breaches', 'ETA at risk'.

List of flagged listings and locked handovers waiting for a decision. Each row shows the item type (Flagged listing or Locked handover), listing reference, donor, reason, time flagged and whether a decision is still open. Selecting a row opens it in the decision panel.

Selected item: listing summary (items, pickup-by, consume-by, status), the flag reason and details, and the time it was raised. Button 'Open listing' links to the listing. Button 'Deactivate donor account' for the listing's donor owner, with a confirmation prompt. Admin decision controls for the item.

Table of rejected and invalid intake calls from the agent call log. Columns: time, call type, the banned claim or injected instruction shown, the outcome (output discarded, template or form used) and review status. Each row has a 'Mark reviewed' button.

Table of offers whose volunteer ETA is later than the deadline minus 15 minutes. Columns: listing reference, receiver, volunteer, volunteer ETA, consume-by deadline, minutes at risk. Each row has a 'Reassign volunteer' button and shows the logged status event after the action.

shows.details: Each item: type, listing reference, donor, reason, details, time raised. Ordered by time raised, oldest first. Locked handovers come from wrong-code lockouts.

shows.item: Listing summary in the decision panel
shows.details: Items, pickup-by time, consume-by deadline, current status, donor name, zone.
Each row: time, call type, banned claim or injected instruction as shown, outcome, reviewed or not.
Each row: listing reference, receiver, assigned volunteer, volunteer ETA, consume-by deadline, gap in minutes. Only offers where ETA is later than deadline minus 15 minutes.
After a reassignment, the new status event for the listing (from, to, actor, time) appears in that row.

actions.action: Select a flagged listing or locked handover and record a decision
actions.result: The item leaves the open queue and the decision is saved with its time.

actions.action: Deactivate the listing donor's account from the decision panel
actions.result: The donor account is deactivated after confirmation; it can be reactivated from Users.

actions.action: Mark a guardrail breach as reviewed
actions.result: The row shows as reviewed with the time and admin.

actions.action: Reassign volunteer on an at-risk offer
actions.result: A volunteer is reassigned, or a receiver collection or donor drop-off is recorded; the logged status event appears in the row.

links.label: Open listing
links.when: Admin wants to see the full listing, handling card and status before deciding on a flag.

links.label: Manage accounts
links.when: After deactivating a donor, admin reviews or reactivates accounts.

states.empty: 'No open flags' in the queue, 'No guardrail breaches' and 'No offers at risk' on their tabs.
states.loading: Skeleton rows in the active tab while the queue, breaches or at-risk offers load.
states.error: A message in the affected tab with a retry button; decisions and reassignments are not shown as saved until the server confirms.

detail.notes: Only the Internal Platform Admin can see or use this screen. The ETA at risk rule is deadline minus 15 minutes. Reassign options are another available volunteer, receiver collection or donor drop-off. Deactivation affects the donor owner's login only. No wording on this screen may call food safe or certified, or mention tax or legal benefits. Synthetic data only; show masked contact details.

detail.purpose: Lets the Internal Platform Admin view and change the assumption values (kg per meal, CO2e emission factor) and the consume-by rule tables, then publish each change as a new numbered version. Every impact number and report states the version it used.

layout.contents: Heading 'Assumptions' with a line saying that changes are versioned and that reports show the version they used.
The version in use: version number, kg per meal, emission factor and its status (estimate range, marked ASSUMPTION until cited), and the rule-table version.
Editable field 'kg per meal' (starting value 0.4); editable field 'emission factor' with its unit and an estimate-range note; a note that each value is an assumption to be cited before demo.
Editable rows of food type, storage, prep time and maximum consume-by limit; an 'Add row' button and a remove control on each row.
Button 'Publish new version' and button 'Discard changes'; shows that publishing creates the next version number and does not overwrite the current one.
List of past versions, newest first, each with its version number, kg per meal, emission factor and rule-table version.

shows.details: Version number, kg per meal, emission factor, rule-table version; the version is the one used by new impact records.
Rows of food type × storage × prep time with the limit they set; the deadline on a listing is the earliest of the donor pickup-by and this limit.
Each past version with its kg per meal, emission factor and rule-table version, newest first.

actions.action: Edit kg per meal or emission factor in the draft
actions.result: The draft shows the new values; the current version stays in use until the draft is published.

actions.action: Add, change or remove a rule-table row in the draft
actions.result: The draft rule table changes; the current rule table stays in use until the draft is published.

actions.action: Publish new version
actions.result: A new numbered AssumptionSet is saved with its values and rule-table version; it becomes the version used for new impact records and reports; earlier versions remain in the history.

actions.action: Discard changes
actions.result: The draft is cleared and the current version is shown again.

states.empty: No rule rows yet: show the starting values as version 1 with an empty rule table and an 'Add row' prompt.
states.loading: Current version, rule table and history load before the form can be edited.
states.error: If publishing fails, nothing is saved as a new version and the draft stays for correction with the error shown.

detail.notes: ['Only the Internal Platform Admin can edit assumptions and rule tables; in the MVP the product owner fills this role.', 'Changes are versioned and never overwrite a published version.', 'Each impact number and report must state the assumption version it used.', 'Emission factor stays labelled ASSUMPTION until a source is cited; show it as an estimate range.', 'Meals saved uses delivered kg only, divided by kg per meal.', 'Not in demo day scope; FR-16 is P1.']

/assumptions.basis: ["Assumptions","Screen to edit assumption values and rule tables, each change versioned.",["Internal Platform Admin"],[["Internal Platform Admin","edit kg per meal, emission factor and rule tables; publish a new version"]]]

detail.purpose: Internal page where the Internal Platform Admin reviews the funnel events and the section 4 success metrics computed from them, for a chosen period or a weekly snapshot. It shows each receiver's share of offers sent.

layout.contents: Heading "Internal metrics" with a line saying the funnel and success metrics are computed from logged status events.
Period selector for the live figures, with a switch to the weekly snapshot and a week picker shown when the snapshot is selected.
Counts for post started, posted, offered, claimed, collected, delivered, expired and cancelled over the chosen period.

Rows for time to post, time to claim, rescue rate, expiry rate, match acceptance and donor retention. Columns: live value, target, and weekly snapshot value when the snapshot is chosen, shown beside the live value.
One row per receiver with offers sent and share of all offers in the chosen period, with a period picker above it.

shows.details: Post started, posted, offered, claimed, collected, delivered, expired, cancelled; counted over the chosen period from the timestamped status-event table.

Time to post (median, target 60 s or less); time to claim (median, target 15 min or less); rescue rate (delivered before deadline ÷ posted, target 70% or more); expiry rate (expired ÷ posted, target under 20%); match acceptance (first offer accepted ÷ first offers, target 50% or more); donor retenti
The same metrics for the chosen week, shown beside the live figures for comparison.
Per receiver: offers sent and share of total offers over the chosen period; fairness is monitored from this share.

actions.action: Choose a period for the live figures
actions.result: Funnel counts, section 4 metrics and receiver share update for that period.

actions.action: Switch to the weekly snapshot and choose a week
actions.result: The weekly figures load and appear beside the live figures.

actions.action: Read each receiver's share of offers sent
actions.result: The per-receiver table shows offers sent and share for the chosen period.

states.empty: No events in the chosen period: counts show zero, metrics show no value, and the receiver table is empty.
states.loading: Figures and tables show a loading indicator while the period or week data loads.
states.error: If the metrics fail to load, a plain message says the figures are unavailable and offers a retry.

detail.notes: Only the Internal Platform Admin may view this page. Figures are computed from logged status events and are not edited here. Targets are the pilot targets from section 4. Metrics that come from elsewhere (LLM golden-set scores, guardrail breaches, demo reliability) are not computed on this page. Share of offers per receiver is monitored for fairness: the reliability weight is capped at 5% and the need weight is 20%.

detail.purpose: Internal page where the Internal Platform Admin checks daily token usage and cost against the budget, and sees when usage reaches the 70% budget alert. It shows the AI spend that intake parsing and report wording generate.

layout.contents: Heading 'Token usage and cost' and a line saying usage is logged per call and reviewed daily.
Shows the share of the token budget used this month. Appears as a warning once usage reaches 70% of budget.
Total tokens used this month, intake tokens, report tokens, estimated cost this month, and cost per listing.
One row per day: date, intake tokens, report tokens, total tokens, and cost for that day.
Intake parsing and impact report wording shown separately, with call count and tokens per call for each.
Planning estimates: about 1,900 tokens per listing and per report, and the per-month totals for the demo, pilot and city-wide scales.

shows.details: Tokens logged for each AI call, split into input and output, grouped by intake parsing and report wording.
Intake tokens, report tokens and total tokens per day, listed by date, most recent first.
Total tokens used this month, with intake and report tokens shown separately.
Percentage of the token budget used, with the 70% alert threshold marked.
Estimated cost per month and per day, calculated as total tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × the model's blended price per million tokens. Cost per listing shown beside it.
Hackathon demo about 0.5 M tokens per month; Bhubaneswar pilot about 3.3 M; city-wide about 31 M.

actions.action: Check today's token usage against the budget
actions.result: Shows the day's and month's tokens and cost, and the budget percentage; if usage is at or above 70%, the alert banner is shown.

states.empty: No AI calls logged yet: all totals show zero and the cost shows as not yet calculated until a price is entered.
states.loading: Totals and the daily table show a loading indicator while usage is fetched.
states.error: A message says usage could not be loaded and asks the admin to refresh; no cost figure is estimated in its place.

detail.notes: Cost is shown only once the model's blended price per million tokens is known (open question Q3). Posts made with the plain form use no AI and do not appear here. Voice posting's speech-to-text charge is priced separately and is not included in these totals. If the budget runs out, AI features stop, but the plain form and template still work (R9). Figures are for internal use by the Internal Platform Admin only.

/usage.basis: ["Usage","Page showing token usage and cost, with the 70% budget alert.",["Internal Platform Admin"],[["Internal Platform Admin","check daily token usage against the budget alert"]]]

detail.purpose: Lets any signed-in or invited person set a new password from the emailed link, and lets a newly added user set their first password. It rejects expired or already-used links.

layout.contents: Heading 'Set a new password' with one line saying the link can be used once and expires.
'New password' field and 'Confirm new password' field, both masked with screen-reader labels, and a 'Save password' button with large tap target.
Hidden until needed. When the link is expired or already used, shows a plain message that the link no longer works, with a 'Request a new link' link.
Replaces the form after a saved password. Says the password is saved and shows a 'Sign in' button.

actions.action: Enters a new password and the same password again, then presses 'Save password'.
actions.result: The password is saved through POST /api/auth/reset-password; the success panel appears and the person can go to sign in.

actions.action: Opens a link that is expired or already used and presses 'Save password'.
actions.result: The request is rejected; no password changes; the link problem message appears with a way to request a new link.

actions.action: Newly added user opens the invitation link and sets their first password.
actions.result: Same as a reset: the password is saved and they go on to sign in.

links.label: Sign in
links.when: After the new password is saved, to sign in with it.

states.empty: The form is shown with empty password fields when a valid link is opened.
states.loading: The save button is disabled and shows progress while the request runs.
states.error: Mismatched passwords or a rejected expired or reused link show a plain message beside the form; no password is changed.

detail.notes: Expired and reused links must be rejected. The screen is reached from the emailed link, so it does not ask for the old password. Newly added users set their first password here as well. Form must work one-handed on a 360 px wide screen with large tap targets and screen-reader labels on both fields.

/reset-password.basis: ["Reset Password","Sets a new password from the emailed link using POST /api/auth/reset-password, rejecting expired or reused links; also how newly added users set their first password.",["CSR Sponsor","Caterer Manager","Internal Platform Admin","NGO / Shelter / Community Kitchen Coordinator","Volunteer Driver"],[]]
